title: Is there a best time to exercise
titleChinese: 一天中有没有最佳的锻炼身体时间？
paragraphs: With our already busy lives, finding time to exercise can feel like one more thing on our ‘to do’ list. So maybe it would help if there was ‘a best time’ to exercise? Could exercising at certain times help maximise our fitness goals? The answer is ‘yes’, but it’s easier than you think – no matter who you are, or when you like to work out.

There are clear benefits to exercising in the morning. Many of us have more free time compared to later in the day, and it may therefore be easier for us to stick to a morning workout routine. A study published in Medicine and Science in Sports and Exercise found that participants who exercised in the morning, increased their physical activity throughout the day, were less distracted by food, and slept better. Exercising on an empty stomach before breakfast could also burn more fat and increase metabolism, which means you’ll continue to burn calories throughout the day.

So, good news for early birds, but what if you’re not a morning person? Working out in the afternoon or evening also has benefits, just different ones. For example, your body’s ability to perform peaks in the afternoon, according to a 2010 study by the Scandinavian Journal of Medicine and Science in Sports. Also, in the afternoon and evening, your reaction time is quickest, and your heart rate and blood pressure are lowest, which reduce your chance of injury while improving performance.

But does any of this change depending on whether you’re a man or a woman? Our bodies are different, after all, so the best time to exercise may be different too. A 2022 study from Skidmore College, New York, looked at exactly this question and the results showed that there are some differences. Want to reduce your blood pressure and you’re a woman? Exercise in the morning. Want to improve your heart health and you’re a man? Evening is better for you. But, ultimately, the study found that there are clear benefits for both sexes to exercising at either time of day.
So what time is best? It seems the answer is: whatever time is best for you!

vocabulary.entry: maximise /ˈmæksɪmaɪz/ v. 使（数量、程度、效果等）最大化；充分利用
vocabulary.example: We need to maximise the efficiency of the production process.
vocabulary.translation: 我们需要最大限度地提高生产流程的效率。

vocabulary.entry: fitness /ˈfɪtnəs/ n. 体能；健身水平；身体健康状况
vocabulary.example: Regular exercise is essential for maintaining good fitness.
vocabulary.translation: 规律运动对于保持良好的体能至关重要。

vocabulary.entry: goal /ɡəʊl/ n. 目标；目的
vocabulary.example: She set herself a fitness goal to run a marathon within two years.
vocabulary.translation: 她为自己定下了两年内跑完马拉松的健身目标。

vocabulary.entry: work out /wɜːk aʊt/ v. 锻炼；健身；做运动
vocabulary.example: I usually work out at the gym three times a week.
vocabulary.translation: 我通常一周去健身房锻炼三次。

vocabulary.entry: stick to /stɪk tuː/ v. 坚持（计划、习惯、决定等）；固守
vocabulary.example: It’s hard to stick to a training plan when you’re busy.
vocabulary.translation: 忙碌的时候很难坚持训练计划。

vocabulary.entry: workout routine /ˈwɜːkaʊt ruːˈtiːn/ n. 常规健身安排；健身计划
vocabulary.example: His workout routine includes running, weight training and yoga.
vocabulary.translation: 他的常规健身安排包括跑步、力量训练和瑜伽。

vocabulary.entry: physical activity /ˈfɪzɪkl ækˈtɪvəti/ n. 身体活动；体育运动
vocabulary.example: Doing more physical activity can lower the risk of chronic diseases.
vocabulary.translation: 多进行身体活动可以降低患慢性病的风险。

vocabulary.entry: distracted by /dɪˈstræktɪd baɪ/ 被……分心；因……无法专注
vocabulary.example: She finds it hard to study and is easily distracted by background noise.
vocabulary.translation: 她很难专心学习，很容易被背景噪音分心。

vocabulary.entry: on an empty stomach /ɒn ən ˈempti ˈstʌmək/ 空腹；没吃东西
vocabulary.example: Do not take this medication on an empty stomach.
vocabulary.translation: 切勿空腹服用此药。

vocabulary.entry: burn fat /bɜːn fæt/ 燃烧脂肪；消耗脂肪
vocabulary.example: High-intensity exercise is a great way to burn fat quickly.
vocabulary.translation: 高强度运动是快速燃烧脂肪的好方法。

vocabulary.entry: metabolism /məˈtæbəlɪzəm/ n. 新陈代谢；代谢作用
vocabulary.example: Eating protein can help boost your metabolism.
vocabulary.translation: 吃蛋白质有助于促进新陈代谢。

vocabulary.entry: burn calories /bɜːn ˈkælərɪz/ 消耗卡路里；燃烧热量
vocabulary.example: Walking for an hour can burn around 200 calories.
vocabulary.translation: 步行一小时大约能消耗200卡路里。

vocabulary.entry: early bird /ˈɜːli bɜːd/ n.（口语）早起的人；早到者
vocabulary.example: I’m not an early bird – I struggle to get up before 8 a.m.
vocabulary.translation: 我不是个早起的人，早上8点前起床对我来说很难。

vocabulary.entry: morning person /ˈmɔːnɪŋ ˈpɜːsn/ n.（口语）晨型人；喜欢早起、早上状态好的人
vocabulary.example: She’s a real morning person and is most productive before lunch.
vocabulary.translation: 她是个典型的晨型人，午饭前的工作效率最高。

vocabulary.entry: ability to perform /əˈbɪləti tu pəˈfɔːm/ n. 表现能力；运动执行能力
vocabulary.example: Proper warm-up can greatly improve an athlete’s ability to perform.
vocabulary.translation: 充分的热身能大幅提升运动员的赛场表现能力。

vocabulary.entry: peak /piːk/ v. 达到顶峰；处于最佳状态；达到最大值
vocabulary.example: Your energy levels usually peak in the late afternoon.
vocabulary.translation: 人的精力通常在傍晚达到顶峰。

vocabulary.entry: Scandinavian /ˌskændɪˈneɪviən/ adj. 斯堪的纳维亚的（北欧挪威、瑞典、丹麦、冰岛等国的）
vocabulary.example: Scandinavian design is known for its simplicity and functionality.
vocabulary.translation: 斯堪的纳维亚设计以简约和实用著称。

vocabulary.entry: reaction time /riˈækʃn taɪm/ n. 反应时间；反应速度
vocabulary.example: Playing fast games can help improve your reaction time.
vocabulary.translation: 玩快节奏的游戏有助于提升反应速度。

vocabulary.entry: heart rate /hɑːt reɪt/ n. 心率
vocabulary.example: Your heart rate increases when you exercise strenuously.
vocabulary.translation: 剧烈运动时心率会加快。

vocabulary.entry: blood pressure /blʌd ˈpreʃə(r)/ n. 血压
vocabulary.example: Regular exercise can help keep your blood pressure under control.
vocabulary.translation: 规律运动有助于控制血压。

vocabulary.entry: reduce the chance of injury /rɪˈdjuːs ðə tʃɑːns ɒv ˈɪndʒəri/ 降低受伤几率；减少受伤可能性
vocabulary.example: Stretching before exercise can reduce the chance of injury.
vocabulary.translation: 运动前拉伸可以降低受伤几率。

vocabulary.entry: improve performance /ɪmˈpruːv pəˈfɔːməns/ 提升表现；改善运动成绩
vocabulary.example: Regular training is the key to improving athletic performance.
vocabulary.translation: 规律训练是提升运动表现的关键。

vocabulary.entry: ultimately /ˈʌltɪmətli/ adv. 最终；归根结底；最后
vocabulary.example: Ultimately, success depends on hard work and persistence.
vocabulary.translation: 成功归根结底取决于努力和坚持。

sentences.english: With our already busy lives, finding time to exercise can feel like one more thing on our ‘to do’ list.
sentences.chinese: 在本就忙碌的生活里，挤出时间运动仿佛成了待办清单上又一项负担。

sentences.english: So maybe it would help if there was ‘a best time’ to exercise?
sentences.chinese: 那么，如果存在一个“最佳运动时间”，会不会让这件事变得更容易？

sentences.english: Could exercising at certain times help maximise our fitness goals?
sentences.chinese: 在特定时间运动，能否帮助我们更高效地达成健身目标？

sentences.english: The answer is ‘yes’, but it’s easier than you think – no matter who you are, or when you like to work out.
sentences.chinese: 答案是肯定的，但这件事比你想象的要简单——无论你是谁，无论你喜欢在什么时段锻炼。

sentences.english: There are clear benefits to exercising in the morning.
sentences.chinese: 早上运动有着显而易见的好处。

sentences.english: Many of us have more free time compared to later in the day, and it may therefore be easier for us to stick to a morning workout routine.
sentences.chinese: 相比一天中的其他时段，我们很多人早上的空闲时间更多，因此也更容易坚持晨练的习惯。

sentences.english: A study published in Medicine and Science in Sports and Exercise found that participants who exercised in the morning, increased their physical activity throughout the day, were less distracted by food, and slept better.
sentences.chinese: 一项发表在《运动医学与科学》期刊上的研究发现，早上运动的参与者，在一天当中的身体活动量会有所增加，对食物的注意力会降低，睡眠质量也会更好。

sentences.english: Exercising on an empty stomach before breakfast could also burn more fat and increase metabolism, which means you’ll continue to burn calories throughout the day.
sentences.chinese: 早餐前空腹运动，还能燃烧更多脂肪并提升新陈代谢，这意味着你在一整天里都会持续消耗卡路里。

sentences.english: So, good news for early birds, but what if you’re not a morning person?
sentences.chinese: 所以这对早起的人来说是个好消息，但如果你不习惯早起该怎么办呢？

sentences.english: Working out in the afternoon or evening also has benefits, just different ones.
sentences.chinese: 下午或晚上运动有与上午运动不同的好处。

sentences.english: For example, your body’s ability to perform peaks in the afternoon, according to a 2010 study by the Scandinavian Journal of Medicine and Science in Sports.
sentences.chinese: 例如，据《斯堪的纳维亚运动医学与科学期刊》2010年的一项研究显示，人体的运动表现能力在下午会达到峰值。

sentences.english: Also, in the afternoon and evening, your reaction time is quickest, and your heart rate and blood pressure are lowest, which reduce your chance of injury while improving performance.
sentences.chinese: 此外，在下午和晚上，人的反应速度最快，心率和血压也处于最低水平，这既能降低受伤风险，又能提升运动表现。

sentences.english: But does any of this change depending on whether you’re a man or a woman?
sentences.chinese: 但这些结论会因性别不同而有所变化吗？

sentences.english: Our bodies are different, after all, so the best time to exercise may be different too.
sentences.chinese: 毕竟男女的身体结构存在差异，那么运动的最佳时间或许也不尽相同。

sentences.english: A 2022 study from Skidmore College, New York, looked at exactly this question and the results showed that there are some differences.
sentences.chinese: 纽约斯基德莫尔学院2022年的一项研究就针对这个问题展开了调查，结果显示确实存在一些差异。

sentences.english: Want to reduce your blood pressure and you’re a woman? Exercise in the morning. Want to improve your heart health and you’re a man? Evening is better for you.
sentences.chinese: 如果你是女性，想要降低血压，那就选择早上运动；如果你是男性，想要改善心脏健康，晚上运动则更适合你。

sentences.english: But, ultimately, the study found that there are clear benefits for both sexes to exercising at either time of day.
sentences.chinese: 不过该研究最终也指出，无论男女，在一天中的任意时段运动，都能收获显著的益处。
那么到底什么时间运动最好呢？

sentences.english: It seems the answer is: whatever time is best for you!
sentences.chinese: 答案似乎是：最适合你的时间，就是最佳时间！
